findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine’s final rinse concentration was tested at 0ppm (CL). Dish machine was ran a few times and still tested at 0ppm. Discussed with PIC and the service tech was contacted to service the dish machine. PIC noted that technician will be to service the machine the following morning. Ensure that the dish machine’s concentration is maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to properly sanitize. Facility will be using the triple sink to sanitize dishes until the dish machine is fixed. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 None of the staff working upon arrival of inspector had a manager certification. Owner arrived during inspection and has a current CFM. The need for additional staff to obtain food manager certification was discussed, and information was provided for food manager courses.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Beans, chili, and cheese sauce in hot holding wells were observed with internal temperatures at 125F-132F. Cook noted all foods were properly reheated and/or had an initial heat this morning on the stove prior to placing in hot holding units. It would appear temperature loss occurred based on when water was added to holding wells and/or lack of water. All products were reheated to 165F/above prior to placing back in hot holding units. Best practices for hot holding were discussed. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Container of shredded potatoes in an ice bath on cook line had an internal temperature of 39F for product in the bottom in contact with ice bath. Product further up in the container that was not in contact with ice bath was observed with an internal temperature ranging from 58F-62F. Potatoes were removed from cook line and placed in the walk-in freezer to quickly chill prior to cold holding in the prep cooler up front. Best practices were discussed for use of ice baths to cold hold TCS foods.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Tuna salad was observed with a date mark of 5/8 in the bottom of a prep cooler at the cook line. Chicken salad had a date mark that was partially torn making it difficult to know the date of prep. Products in question were discarded. 
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Portion of sliced potatoes were observed with surface and internal temperatures of 104F and 88F respectively. Potatoes were blanched in the fryer ~30 minutes prior to temperature check. Potatoes were in a covered container on ice at the cook line, but only the bottom of the container was in contact with ice intended for chilling. Potatoes were removed from the cook line and placed in the walk-in freezer to quickly chill product. Best practices were discussed for quick chilling cooked TCS foods.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. Food handler certifications were not available for staff working at the facility longer than 30 days. Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course within 30 days of hiring, and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Owner does not currently have an allergen certification. Owner plans to complete online food allergen certification and have additional staff complete certification to ensure enough staff have certifications in conjunction with food manager certification.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Observed the dish machine and sani buckets to measure at 0 ppm of bleach. The dish machine and sani buckets must maintain concentrations between 50 and 200 ppm of bleach to properly sanitize food contact surfaces. The sani buckets were changed during the inspection, and a technician from MJ Kellner arrived to fix the dish machine, and the sanitizer measured 100 ppm after it was serviced.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed a container of cottage cheese dated 01/07/2020. This exceeds the 7 day date marking policy. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Food was discarded during the inspection. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.comment:
Light shield on cooler broken.

750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed shell eggs above ready to eat products in the prep cooler. Observed turkeys above ground beef and par cooked bacon in the walk in cooler. Store foods in proper order according to cooking temperatures.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed a container of brown granule to be near the back dry storage shelf without proper labeling. All items removed from their original container must be labeled with the common name of the product.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed house made tuna and egg salads in the prep cooler to be date marked 9/1. Yesterday would have been the last day to use these within the 7 days. The date of preparation counts as Day 1 and must be discarded at 7 days (i.e. Monday - Sunday usage). There was also tomato soup dated 8/31. It is believed that these were pulled from the freezer today, but were not re-dated. All of these items were discarded during the inspection.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed mashed potatoes on the steam table to be probed at an internal temperature of 125F. Steam table was adjusted as it is reported that these potatoes had only been on the steam table for about an hour. Bacon on the steam table was only around 100F as well and this bacon was not fully cooked to be crisp. It was discussed that bacon is not potentially hazardous if it is cooked fully to crisp, otherwise it needs to be held at 41F or below or 135F or above.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
1) Observed green chili and red chili on the bottom shelf in the 2 door reach in cooler to be probed at internal temperatures of 46 and 48F respectively. All other items in the cooler were within allowable temperatures. Monitor this cooler and the chili to ensure that these foods are being held at 41F or below. Chili was discarded during the inspection. 2) Observed a bottle of au jus dated 2/18 and a small container of grits, an open container of chicken salad and an open container of tuna salad in the prep cooler to not be date marked. Date mark all ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods with the date that they are opened and hold no longer than 7 days. These items were reported to have been opened a couple days ago and were date marked as such.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.comment:
Observed gravy on the steam table in the kitchen to be probed at an internal temperature of 124F. Gravy was reported to have been on a double boiler on the stove top before being placed on the steam table, but it was reported that they got busy and needed the space on the stove top so it was transferred to the steam table approximately 15 minutes ago. Items from the steam table were pulled and reheated on the stove to 165F before being placed back in the steam table. Do not use the steam table to reheat. All items must be reheated on the stove rapidly to 165 before being hot held at 135F or above.
750-210  Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165°F or higher through out the product. Properly reheat food to 165°F or above.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:

750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee touch his hat and then put on gloves to return to the cook line. Anytime hands may become contaminated, they must be washed for a full 20 seconds with soap and water and paper towels should be used to turn off the faucet. Hands should also be washed in between changes in task and not just changing gloves.
750-510a Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.
